extracted.intended_audience: Action Editors (AEs) and prospective editors for the Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR) journal
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Action Editors handling submission prescreening, reviewer assignment, post-review discussion, decision-making, and camera-ready checks for the DMLR journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescreening timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a week after your assignment as an Action Editor (AE), your duties begin by evaluating whether the submission successfully clears the pre-screening stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the submission within one week of assignment; if uncertain about borderline cases, seek guidance from the Editors-in-Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescreening criteria — desk rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission breaches the DMLR LaTeX style guidelines and/or the NeurIPS Code of Ethics or falls out of alignment with DMLR's scope, and if it clearly fails to meet DMLR's journal standards, it should be desk-rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desk-reject when there is a clear breach of style, ethics, scope, or journal standards. For ambiguous cases consult the Editors-in-Chief rather than desk-rejecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirming pre-screen and public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission successfully passes the pre-screening, you may confirm this via your OpenReview console. Subsequently, the submission will be made accessible to the public, and your identity as the responsible AE will be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the OpenReview confirmation mechanism to move a submission past prescreen; be aware that confirming publicly reveals the submission and the AE identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment — number and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: After confirming a submission's suitability for the DMLR Journal, you should proceed to assign three reviewers to review the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initially reach out to reviewers whose judgment you have confidence in. If needed, DMLR can provide contact information of interested reviewers. Members of the public who volunteer may be accepted at the AE's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review duration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers that are shorter than 25 pages (excluding the Appendix and supplementary documents), the expected review period is one month. For longer papers, the Action Editor (AE) may determine an appropriate review duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1 month as the default timeline for <25-page submissions; set a reasonable extended timeline for longer papers. DMLR prioritizes quality of reviews over speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizing review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR prioritizes the quality of reviews over speediness. As such, the decision on whether the reviews meet the required quality standards rests with the AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AE is responsible for judging whether submitted reviews are sufficiently thorough and informative; if reviews are inadequate, the AE should recruit additional reviewers or take steps to improve review quality before making decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review discussion duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all the reviews have been submitted, they will become visible to other reviewers, and you can initiate the post-review discussion phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate and moderate the discussion; expect reviewers to actively engage, collaborate to reach consensus on recommendations, and ask targeted questions to authors when appropriate. Use this phase to align on whether the submission meets the Acceptance Criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Acceptance Criteria and Reviewer Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you proceed, please review the Reviewer Guidelines, Acceptance Criteria and Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs must be familiar with the journal's Reviewer Guidelines, formal Acceptance Criteria, and Code of Conduct and use them to guide prescreening, reviewer evaluation, and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling ethical concerns — flagging for Ethical Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Should you have concerns regarding the ethical implications of a submission, you have the option to flag it for Ethical Review on OpenReview, in accordance with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics that we closely adhere to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag ethically concerning submissions on OpenReview to notify Editors-in-Chief; an Ethics Reviewer will be assigned to assess ethical issues. Use the NeurIPS Code of Ethics as a reference for ethical flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision authority and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion phase concludes when you make a final decision for the paper, which can be either an acceptance or a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs make the final decision (accept/reject). For accepted papers, you may request minor revisions for camera-ready; for rejections, promptly notify authors. Ensure decisions reflect consensus and alignment with Acceptance Criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, authors are required to provide a 'camera-ready' version incorporating the requested revisions if applicable. This camera-ready version must adhere to the DMLR LaTeX style guidelines and include a link to the paper's review page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the camera-ready document follows the DMLR LaTeX style and includes the review-page link. Encourage submission of supplementary materials (datasets, appendices, audio/visual presentations, code) that support the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE core responsibilities summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Action Editors (AEs) have a central importance in ensuring the accepted papers are up to standards of best practices in data-centered machine learning research. Briefly, AEs are responsible for prescreening assigned submissions, recruiting reviewers for submissions that pass prescreening, ensuring that all submissions receive quality reviews, facilitating discussions among reviewers, evaluating the quality of reviews, making decision recommendations, and making sure the camera-ready papers are ready to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfill each duty end-to-end: prescreen promptly, recruit appropriate reviewers, ensure review quality, drive and moderate post-review discussion, apply Acceptance Criteria and Ethics policies, render decisions, and verify camera-ready compliance prior to publication.
